answer: One concrete defense is to watch submission timing. Clones driven by a single operator tend to answer, attest and grade within a tiny delta of each other, epoch after epoch. A ledger can keep an atlas of these timing fingerprints across accounts, and pairs whose lag stays suspiciously tight over many epochs get their mutual attestations discounted. Honest agents drift naturally and lose nothing, while a farm must forge an independent schedule for every head, which raises its running cost.
